sections.pages: Book p.72 to 73 · Workbook p.56 to 57

learn.title: Where does chocolate come from? (short summary)
lines: Read the full text on page 72 in your book.
🌳 Chocolate comes from big pods that grow on the cacao tree. Farmers open the pods and take out the seeds.
🧂 Later, vanilla, sugar, cinnamon and other spices are added. That's why it tastes so delicious!
☕ Two thousand years ago, chocolate was a drink. Later, people learned to change it from liquid to solid.
🍫 In 1847, Joseph Fry invented chocolate candy bars. Today there are thousands of types!
🎉 International Chocolate Day is on September 13.

sections.title: Grammar 1: Past progressive

learn.title: An action in progress in the past
lines: Use the past progressive for an action that was happening at a time in the past.
At 8 p.m. last night, I was watching TV. 📺
examples: By 250 CE, people were drinking hot chocolate.
The cacao tree was growing in Africa by the late 1800s.

learn.title: was / were + verb-ing
table: She was going to the store.

learn.title: Adding -ing
lines: Most verbs: add -ing → eating, sleeping
Ends in e: drop the e → living, making
Short verb, vowel + consonant: double it → winning, swimming

learn.title: Past progressive + when + simple past
lines: A long action was happening when a short action interrupted it.
━━━━ was drinking ━━━━ ⚡ burned
examples: I was drinking hot chocolate when I burned my hand!
We were talking about chocolate when I remembered the candy bar in my backpack.

sections.title: Grammar 2: Cause and effect with so that

learn.title: so that = for this reason 🎯
lines: Use so that to give the reason for an action.
CAUSE (what I did) + so that + EFFECT (why I did it)
examples: The boy printed out the recipe so that he could read it while he was cooking.
We put all the ingredients on the table so that it would be easy to find them later.

learn.title: so that + could / would / wouldn't
lines: After a past verb, use could, would or wouldn't + verb.
table: Wei-Wei put the recipe in front of her
She put a lid on the bowl

learn.title: can → could, will → would
lines: In the past, can becomes could, and will becomes would.
examples: I made a list of ingredients so that I would remember to buy everything.

learn.title: The Story of Chocolate (part 1)
lines: Read the full text in your book. This is a short summary.
🌎 The story starts with the Olmecs and the Mayas in the Americas, more than 1,000 years ago.
☕ The Mayas drank chocolate around 2,600 years ago. They grew cacao trees and used the seeds as money: 10 seeds could buy a rabbit!
🌶️ The Aztecs drank it hot too, and added spices. Rich people drank it at every meal. Later, a rabbit cost 30 seeds.

learn.title: The Story of Chocolate (part 2)
lines: 🇪🇸 In 1519, the Spanish arrived and tried chocolate. They hated it because it was very bitter, so they mixed it with sugar.
⛵ In 1528, the Spanish took the seeds and the recipe back to Spain so that they could drink chocolate there.
Before this, no one in Europe knew about chocolate!
🤯 Weird but true: People say the Aztec ruler Moctezuma II drank 50 cups of chocolate a day!

learn.title: The Sweet World of Art (Workbook p.62)
lines: Read the full text in your workbook. This is a short summary.
Mirco Della Vecchia is an Italian chef and artist. He makes amazing ice cream, chocolate cakes, and chocolate sculptures.
He built small copies of famous sites in chocolate, and he made the largest chocolate sculpture in the world: over 4 meters tall!

lines: Barton Seaver is a chef and a conservationist.
His message: The food we choose to eat every day can help to save the Earth. Read his words on page 79. 📖

learn.title: Read a chocolate label 🏷️
lines: 🔎 Ingredients: cocoa, sugar, milk, vanilla…
🍬 How much sugar is in it?
🌍 Where does the cocoa come from?
🤔 Are there ingredients you don't know? Ask T. Roy!

book.q: Why is it important to learn about the ingredients in your food?
book.answer: So that we can choose healthy food and know what we are eating.

book.q: Find some chocolate wrappers and look at the labels. What can you learn about the chocolate from these labels?
book.answer: We can learn the ingredients, how much sugar it has, and where it was made.

book.q: Which ingredients do you think are unhealthy? Which do you think are healthy? Are there any ingredients that you don't know?
book.answer: I think too much sugar is unhealthy. Milk and nuts are healthy.

models: It's important to learn about our food.
Too much sugar is unhealthy.

turns.q: What healthy food do you like?
turns.example: I like fruit, rice and fish.

turns.q: What food should we eat less of?
turns.example: We should eat less candy and fewer chips.

quiz.q: Barton Seaver is a chef and a ____.

sections.title: Writing: Paragraph Unity

learn.title: What is paragraph unity?
lines: A good paragraph has unity: all the sentences are about the main idea.
The topic sentence gives the main idea. The supporting sentences give details about it.
If a sentence is about something else, cross it out! ✂️

learn.title: Chocolate Customs (short summary)
lines: Read the full blog in your workbook. 📒
🇯🇵 Keiko from Japan: On Valentine's Day, women give chocolate to men. On White Day (March 14), men give chocolate to women.
🇲🇽 Pablo from Mexico: On the Day of the Dead, his family cooks a meal with chocolate sauce and buys chocolate skulls.

learn.title: Plan your paragraph
lines: Topic sentence: In my family, we eat chocolate on special days.
Detail 1: When? (birthdays, New Year, Valentine's Day)
Detail 2: What do you do? (give a box of chocolates, make a cake)
Check: Is every sentence about chocolate on special days? ✅

wb.q: Keiko's blog: cross out three sentences that do not belong.
wb.answer: The history of chocolate is interesting. · International Chocolate Day is in September. · Our school year starts in April.
wb.hint: Keiko's main idea: chocolate on Valentine's Day and White Day in Japan.

wb.q: Pablo's blog: cross out three sentences that do not belong.
wb.answer: Mexico City is the capital of Mexico. · Most supermarkets are open until 9 PM. · I don't like chocolate milkshakes.
wb.hint: Pablo's main idea: how his family uses chocolate on the Day of the Dead.

wb.q: Write about a custom or a special celebration when people use chocolate. Make sure all the sentences are related to the topic.
wb.answer: In my family, we eat chocolate on birthdays. My mom makes a big chocolate cake. We put candles on it and sing "Happy Birthday." Then everyone eats a piece. It is my favorite day of the year!
wb.hint: Use the plan in Learn. Check that every sentence is about your topic.

sort.title: Topic: chocolate on Valentine's Day. Does the sentence belong?
items: Stores sell lots of chocolate in February.
Our school year starts in April.
The capital of Japan is Tokyo.
